questions.question: How important was the Hoare-Laval Pact in destroying the League's credibility? (8 marks)

points.text: The Hoare-Laval Pact was very important in destroying the League's credibility. It revealed that Britain and France - the League's most powerful members - were secretly willing to give Italy most of Abyssinia, completely betraying the principle of collective security. questions.question: "The League failed because of its structural weaknesses, not because of circumstances." How far do you agree? (16 marks)

points.text: The League failed because of both structural weaknesses and circumstances, but the structural weaknesses were more fundamental. The League had no army, meaning it could never enforce decisions; the USA never joined, removing the world's greatest power; the unanimity rule meant any member could veto action; and Britain and France were not genuinely committed.
